plugin.name: Jujutsu VCS Integration
plugin.description:
Native IntelliJ integration for Jujutsu (jj), a Git-compatible version control system with a fundamentally different approach to working with code.

Why Jujutsu?

Jujutsu treats your working copy as a commit—always. No staging area, no "dirty" state. Just describe what you're working on and keep coding.

Key Features

  • Describe-First Workflow — Working Copy tool window for describing current work and creating new changes.
  • Custom Log View — Visual commit graph with inline change IDs, descriptions, and bookmarks.
  • Change Operations — Edit, abandon, and describe changes directly from the log.
  • File History & Annotations — Full file history with diff viewer and line-by-line blame.
  • Multi-Repository Support — Work with multiple JJ repositories in a single project.
  • Real-Time Status — Auto-refresh keeps the UI in sync as you edit files.

GitHub · Issues
plugin.change-notes:
0.8.17

Added

  • Restore now opens a dialog listing every changed file, with your selection pre-checked but adjustable, instead of a plain Yes/No confirmation — applies to both "Restore" (working copy → parent revision) and "Restore to This" (working copy → a historical revision). A successful restore also now shows an undo balloon with an inline Undo link. ([#84](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/84))
  • New "Move Up"/"Move Down" actions swap the selected commit with its single child or single parent in the commit graph (`jj rebase -A`/`-B`), as a keyboard-first complement to drag-and-drop reordering. Default shortcut Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down on every platform, including macOS - Cmd+Shift+Up/Down is deliberately not used there, since it's already the system shortcut for extending a selection to the top/bottom of a list; also in the log's right-click menu next to Rebase. Disabled when the selection isn't a single commit, doesn't have exactly one child/parent on that side, or the move would touch an immutable commit. ([#93](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/93))
  • The conflicted-file editor banner now reflects jj's own incremental conflict model instead of a static "This file has merge conflicts": it shows a live count of remaining conflict blocks that updates as you hand-edit the markers (and disappears once the last one is gone, without waiting for a save), and offers "Accept " links labelled with jj's own commit descriptions for each side, alongside the existing "Open Merge Tool" link. ([#112](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/112))
  • Visible heads with no bookmark on them — work left behind after a forgotten `jj bookmark advance` — are now surfaced instead of silently sitting unnoticed: the bookmarks panel gets a collapsible "Unbookmarked heads" category (below the "@" row, above Local) listing each one as "\ +n \", double-clickable to jump the log there, and the log table itself marks each such row with a small slashed-bookmark icon. ([#48](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/48), [#107](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/107))

    • Changed

  • The Working Copy tool window now has an icon representing a working copy rather than IntelliJ's default VCS icon ([#101](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/101))

    • Fixed

  • Restore, Show File History, Squash Selected Files, and Split no longer hide themselves for a deleted file selected alone in the Working Copy panel or a commit's changed-files list — a deleted file has no editor-visible content, and that was mistaken for "nothing selected". A selection mixing a deleted file with an edited one now restores both instead of silently dropping the deleted one. ([#122](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/122))
  • The bookmark widget's/bookmarks panel's "\ +N" indicator could show a wildly inflated (or capped, e.g. "+1000+") distance for a merge commit with one bookmarked parent and one unrelated, unbookmarked parent — it was counting the entire unrelated branch's history instead of the actual hops back to the bookmark.
  • Scrolling the (early-access) paged log through a large repo's history got progressively slower the deeper you scrolled — each "Load more" page re-sorted and re-laid-out the entire log loaded so far, not just the new page, turning a scroll to depth N into roughly N² work. Loading a page now extends the previous merge/layout instead of recomputing it from scratch, so a long scroll costs roughly the same total work regardless of how many pages came before. ([#69](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/69))
  • A divergent (conflicted) local bookmark couldn't be moved back onto the change it was already on — the natural way to resolve it — from either "Move Bookmark Here…" or "Move '\' to Change…"; both dialogs assumed a bookmark has exactly one current target and excluded or misclassified it whenever a candidate matched. Every target is now offered, labelled "Resolve conflict", and selectable without ticking "Allow backward or sideways move". "Move '\' to Change…" also now shows an undo balloon and supports Undo after a move, matching every other bookmark-move path. ([#121](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/121))
  • A bookmark whose local ref was pending deletion (`jj bookmark delete`) but whose remote-tracking ref still existed could show a wildly wrong ahead count (e.g. "1000+ commits ahead") in the bookmarks panel — jj reports that count as the distance from the now-absent local ref to the repo root, not a real divergence. The log table already corrected this; the bookmarks panel, and every log-table refresh path past the very first load (paging, Refresh, search), now do too. ([#110](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/110))
  • Toolbar Refresh now also re-reads bookmarks, tags, and working-copy state, not just log rows — previously an external change picked up only by the (unreliable on some network drives) op_heads file watch could leave the bookmark widget, bookmark chips, and reference filter stale even after clicking Refresh. ([#115](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/115))
  • A conflicted file at a historical (non-working-copy) commit whose path contained a space was silently missing its conflict marker in that commit's changes list — the underlying `jj resolve --list` parser now reuses the same shape-aware parser as the working copy instead of a whitespace-splitting one, and populates the conflict registry for that revision too (laying groundwork for a future revision-aware conflicts view).
  • Split's dialog now names the two resulting sides by what they *are* — "Existing commit"/"New commit" — consistently across the description labels, diff preview titles, summary line, and hunk picker, instead of a mix of DAG position ("Parent"/"Child"/"First"/"Second"/"Here") and a mismatched "(keeps change ID)" aside that only appeared on one of them; ticking a file now has the same meaning everywhere. The previous separate bold identity header and plain description sub-label above each description editor are combined into one label ("Description for existing commit (``)" / "Description for new commit (child of / sibling of / parent of ``)"), dropping the redundant "(unchanged unless edited)" aside. A muted note under "Source" states the resulting shape, leading with the same "existing commit" naming, including that existing children become merges of both siblings in a parallel split, and word-wraps instead of forcing the dialog's left column wider. Every change id shown in these labels now uses the same bold-prefix/grey-remainder styling as the rest of the plugin. Toggling "Create parallel commits" also now relabels the description labels, note, and summary immediately, instead of only on the next file-tick. ([#101](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/101), [#114](https://github.com/kkkev/jj-idea/issues/114))

    • See full release notes for details.
